#4132. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4131. GTA 6: How to Unlock the Apartment Laptop in Chapter 3

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of those games that has seemingly infinite things to do. There are the main quests, side quests, side activities and then there are hidden quests that you can’t track in a standard in-game journal.

When you get to Vice City in chapter 3, you will be housed in a full “furnished” apartment, meaning that the last tenant up and left all their stuff. With it, though, you’ll be able to go through her stuff, including her personal laptop, if you’re able to find the password.

Find a fighter jet in GTA 6, learn how to enter Mile Zero Air Station, and escape the five-star wanted level after stealing one.

All of the clues are found within the apartment itself, so you’ll just need to do some exploring.

This will give you the clues you need. This girl was obsessed with her dog and used him as her password:

The dog’s name is Muffins, she drew her as a queen on the notepad, and on the back of the notepad is the class of ’15 reunion reminder. With that, you can search the computer. The important tab is in WhatUp with the Unknown user, where they will give Vanessa a password to a place.

The next step in this surprisingly hidden side quest is finding the keypad that’s assigned to this keycode. Thankfully, there are a couple of hints that are given in the original email:

The first part is pretty self-explanatory as there’s a district to the south of the apartment that’s called La Perle. You’ll go there to meet Tyrone. Near Auntie’s is a little more difficult only because you need to find environmental clues.

Head into town and then look for Tyrone’s place. If you haven’t gotten to this part yet, which is the first mission into chapter 3, look for the clothing thrift store on the map. From Tyrone’s place, head south one block and on the right, you’ll find a restaurant called Auntie’s Soul Food. There will be a parking lot behind this building and slightly to the north. Head there and enter the code on the panel.

Surprisingly, there are two different rewards in this quest. For starters, you will get the Growler vehicle for free. If you want to sell it, it will get you $14,750, which isn’t anything to scoff at. With that said, only really sell it if you desperately need space in your garages.

The more important reward, though, is that the garage that you opened with the keypad is now yours to keep. There is an additional one car, on top of being able to go there to sell marked bills, jewelry and narcotics. There’s also a weapons locker in the back, which is a little more important given Tyrone is nearby for stuff to sell.

#4130. Fnatic confirms Razork exit as Lospa’s SK Gaming move deepens 2027 rebuild

Fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

Fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

The club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

His next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

The rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

That deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

The overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

5 years of memories. it was an honour to see you grow into the person and player you are 🧡 https://t.co/F3TWY9WZqq pic.twitter.com/K3K3EQICZ1

For the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

The club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert says Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The new hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

#4129. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4128. GTA 6: Should You Shoot or Spare Felipe

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Choice is a huge component in a lot of games, and it has always had an impact in Grand Theft Auto. In Grand Theft Auto 6, there are various missions and side quests where you will be able to not only play stealthily but be restrained in how you approach a situation. It isn’t always about guns blazing but also talking your way out of a situation.

For Felipe, he probably deserves what comes to him, but if you put away your itchy trigger finger, you will find that there is a greater reward.

Should you sell pure product or Tyrone’s cut batch in GTA 6? Compare the outcomes, risks, and rewards of each Dealer’s Choice option.

If you have gotten this far and don’t know what Felipe did to deserve to be shot or spared, then it’s best you turn back. This is a significant spoiler near the end of chapter 3 of Grand Theft Auto 6.

With that said, Felipe essentially bailed on the plan by Raul, resulting in the death of Nicole. Andrea especially isn’t too happy about it and gets information that Felipe is still in town and a general area of where you can look to find him.

He is located all the way up in the north in Millport, so drive or fly all the way up there and pay him a visit. When you get to a local bar, enter and start asking around for him. Eventually, he will come out of the back and immediately recognize you, initiating a chase. Chase him down only for Lucia to tackle him. Now it’s time to confront him.

Now that you have caught up to the backstabber who threw off the entire plan, you have to deal with him. You are able to question him, but in the end, he will just respond with requests to just get it over with.

Shooting Felipe will essentially get you nothing but the satisfaction of taking out someone who screwed you.

Now that you have cooled your head, there is another option for Felipe: sparing him. Depending on how you play the game, maybe this isn’t for you, but there is a benefit to letting him live.

Jason will tell him to get out of here and that killing him will change nothing. If you change your mind, he does walk away very slowly giving you a chance to reconsider. With that said, you do get rewarded.

After texting Andrea that you couldn’t find Felipe, Felipe will text you. He will thank you for letting him go and left you a bike at the old church by Lost Heaven Cemetery. In the end, you will get rewarded with a new set of wheels. Not bad for restraining yourself.

#4126. Pikmin 4 Is Still Great, But Dandori Academy Is Underwhelming

Pikmin 4 was released for the original Switch in 2023, and it ranks among my favorite games on the platform; I happily award it the honor of being the best Pikmin game. It looks and plays great, and Oatchi the dog makes the sometimes annoying process of managing a collection of little plant creatures willing to do your bidding much smoother.

The over-titled Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy releases November 12, and much like other comparable Nintendo games that have been ported and improved for Switch 2 (like Kirby and Mario Party), the base game is as good as it was initially and looks even better. If you skipped Pikmin 4 on Switch for whatever reason (probably because it was day one of the Barbenheimer epidemic), I encourage you to play it now. You have about a week to beat it before… something else comes out. Who’s to say.

The “big” addition here for the Switch 2 version of the game, alongside improved performance and visuals and the ability to give Oatchi verbal commands, is Dandori Academy. The Academy is an expanded time trial mode that awards medals for practicing specific levels, which you can then play and upload your high scores on specific days. For example, I can play the Advanced B level, Rockaway Cellars, as much as I want, but it only really counts if I play it on November 12. And you only get one try (though you can unlock retry tickets).

In theory, I like the unique approach to high-score battling, and the limited timeframe adds fun intensity, but this isn't what I am looking for from Pikmin. I recognize and acknowledge the design decision to place timers on your interactions in Pikmin, but it’s never been my favorite part. I like building my adorable little army and exploring, discovering, and retrieving as many unexpected items as possible. But I mostly get annoyed at the ticking clock, especially when I am watching my crew meander toward my spaceship holding a Game Boy Advance SP (or whatever they manage to find on the never-acknowledged, but potentially post-apocalyptic Earth you are exploring).

I also like having a list of missions to complete, and in Dandori Academy, there isn’t much acknowledgment of your success in practice. You can earn a platinum medal while practicing Rockaway Cellar, but it’s mainly to let you know that this is what you could earn when you play on the right day.

The main takeaway is that Pikmin 4 is still excellent, and I was grateful to transfer my save file from the Switch version (and I was tempted to start a new game + save), but Dandori Academy is not a strong incentive to return if you already played the game. It is a nice bonus and an interesting concept that reimagines the familiar time trial mode featured in plenty of video games, but the original campaign is still the main attraction.

#4125. Nongshim RedForce sign Deft after military service, reuniting DRX’s 2022 world title trio

Nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik. The move follows an eighth-place 2026 for the club and comes days after BLG ended Korea's four-year hold on the World Championship.

Kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November. The club used its official social media channels to make the announcement. Deft began his military service after the 2024 season ended.

The deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship. Jungler Hong ‘Pyosik’ Chang-hyeon joined later the same day, alongside support Moon ‘Andil’ Gwan-bin. Top laner Hwang ‘Kingen’ Seong-hoon had re-signed a day earlier.

Deft’s signing was announced at 7pm. The Pyosik and Andil additions that followed completed Nongshim’s five-man starting line-up, Inven Global reported. Mid laner Seon ‘Calix’ Hyeon-bin provides continuity. He has been with the organisation since 2021 and extended his deal on 18 November.

Deft brings a long winning record. He made his debut with MVP Blue in 2013. His titles include the LCK, the LPL, the Mid-Season Invitational and the 2022 World Championship.

Kingen first joined Nongshim for the 2025 season. Pyosik arrives after a difficult 2026 at DN SOOPers. That team lost a run of matches, and rookie Sharvel took his starting place.

The move had been signalled. About a month before the announcement, Sheep Esports reported from Korean sources that Nongshim planned to sign Deft. The same report said rookie AD carry Diable would need a new team.

The signings mark a sharp change of direction after a poor year. Once the league campaign was over, the team lasted just a single match in the play-ins.

#4122. GTA 6: How to Identify Which Houses You Can Enter

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Theft is in the name, so what better way to plan a good heist than to have a good understanding of how the map system works in Grand Theft Auto 6? Well, thankfully, we have the solution for you. If you are wondering if you’re able to enter a specific property, there is an easy and handy way to identify it on the map. This guide will go over just how to do so.

Explore the money-making methods covered in this GTA 6 guide, from side activities and selling cars to store robberies and bank heists.

There’s a surprisingly well-designed feature in the map that no one really ever tells you about. Rockstar has created both a 2D and 3D virtual map for you to set waypoints, filter certain facilities and see where you haven’t been yet.

One aspect of it is color. The coloring scheme is very handy not only in the open world (especially during your focus), but also in the map. By opening up a map, you will find essentially two different colors for houses and structures.

If a structure is light blue, that means you won’t be able to get inside. If that structure is dark blue, that means you’ll be able to enter it. This can be done either through a doorway (where you can use a Snap Gun to avoid alarms or breaking in through brute force), or through a garage.

With that said, not every dark blue structure can be accessed only because there are some that are tied specifically to the story and side missions. You will be able to move around in these houses during these quests but not in the open world.

One of the best parts of Grand Theft Auto 6 is just exploring. Rockstar has created a breathtaking world to adventure, be it through the various missions or just going out on your own and creating havoc for yourself.

There are two aspects to why you’d go through these houses. The first is obviously to rob them or find collectibles. This is very much encouraged for more bigger locations such as banks, stores and so forth.

For standard houses, it’s all about environmental storytelling. Whether it’s coming across a house with what looks like a person who was recently tortured, a house with a disturbing number of female mannequins in it or a football player with a ton of trophies and footballs on display, Rockstar has created a fantastic world to just poke your nose in.

#4121. Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his plan.

As for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

#4118. GTA 6: How to Get into the Airport

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Whether it’s driving around the vast city skyline of Vice City, boating in the Pacific Ocean or taking to the skies, there’s no shortage of ways to see Grand Theft Auto 6 in all of its beauty. While you won’t be taking planes to Liberty City or Los Santos, you can break into the airport and steal a plane.

There are a couple of ways to get into the airport, not one being through the arrivals or departure terminals. To start things off, you will need to know where it’s located. The VCIA (Vice City International Airport) is located near the middle of the map, just west of the Salton district.

Probably the easiest way to get in is flying in from a helicopter or from a plane you obtained from the early portions of the game. You will be picked up pretty quickly as the threshold for the radar is low, but it’s definitely the simplest method in finding your way in. Driving in is also an option as there are various checkpoints you can slam right through.

Outside these options, there are some really easy entrances to the airport if you don’t have a plane or helicopter at your disposal. While driving is probably the way to go, there are fences on the east and west portions of the map that can get in from.

Most of it is barbed, but you will find some that is a simple fence to hop over (as shown in the photo). Simply jump over and sneak around. People will notice you if you come in view of them, so steal a vehicle as quick as possible, but even the, they have trackers.

Unfortunately, when you steal a commercial vehicle such as a Dreamliner in Grand Theft Auto 6, things are not going to go well for you. People will immediately notice when an aircraft isn’t supposed to leave and takes off.

If you completed most of chapter 4 of the story, you’ll know that the airport has numerous safety measures, including snipers perched on every corner. On top of that, air traffic control will immediately catch wind of what you’re doing.

Sadly, when you get off the ground, you will be met with multiple stars, and they will immediately call-in fighter jets. If you don’t put the plane down, they will do so forcefully. You will have a limited amount of time to finish your joyride before it’s removed from the air permanently.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

#4115. GTA 6: Where to Find Helicopters

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

How you travel in Grand Theft Auto 6 is very important. Whether it’s by plane, train or automobile, there’s a slew of different ways to get around the vast world Rockstar has created. One of them is a helicopter. This is an iconic vehicle from the franchise that gets you to places faster than most, but securing one isn’t exactly the easiest thing to do. Thankfully, with this guide, you’ll be able to find them with ease.

Getting a helicopter is one of the better ways to travel in Grand Theft Auto 6. While planes are faster and bring you further distances, there isn’t always a good way to park them. You can definitely try landing on some rugged piece of land or on the freeway, but the chances it will work or stay there when you come back is unlikely – not to mention the chances of getting back into the sky are unlikely.

You can definitely jump out and parachute to where you’re going, but then you’ve lost your means of transportation. That’s where helicopters come into play. They are a good middle ground where they can cover a good amount of ground fast and be more versatile when it comes to escape vehicles.

Heck, during robberies, parking this out back is always handy if cops aren’t at the ready when you exit the building. While you’ll be unable to register helicopters as personal vehicles, having a good idea where they are located is always good.

Find out how to get into bank vaults in GTA 6, complete Yasmani’s Lombank robbery, escape the police, and get tips on more vaults.

Early on, there are very few actual helicopters to speak of. You will be able to find a couple of helicopters that can land on water, but even they are rarer than water planes. Where you will need to look is in Vice City itself.

The easiest tell is looking at the map and looking for a helipad. The thing, though, is that not all helipads have helicopters on them. Some are meant for you to land on them instead of housing something for you to take.

You will want to look in three different districts of Vice City: Tequesta, Downtown and Washington Beach, specifically in that order to look for them.

Tequesta has arguably the most to choose from, but we’re assuming you’re coming from the south. From here, there will be a hotel all the way to the southeast of the area up against the water. Enter from the front and take the elevator all the way up.

If you’re coming from the south, the first place you should hit is the Rico Huxley Hotels. This is located on the river just east of the Zenith gym. Take the elevator up into the lobby and then break into the roof access area.

If you’ve made it to the fourth chapter, you’ll be pretty familiar with the area, but the Crimson Palms Condominiums is the place you need to go. This is up against the water to the north, two buildings south of the Aichi Condominiums Outdoor Gym. Like the others, take the elevator up and get onto the roof.

#4113. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

Shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10 UTC on Saturday 21 November, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

The result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that said it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

The Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

Shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

The organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

The prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has a wide variety of encounters that can crop up across its central locales. While most are tied to a specific area or mission, some of the game’s most memorable are those that can occur anywhere within a given zone, adding tons of random madness to Leonida while free-roaming.

Tales of streakers were some of the first leaks to breach GTA 6, and those on the hunt may be a bit disappointed.

Many of these quests are direct references to other pieces of crime fiction, from subtle hints to straight-up placing the protagonists in the situation from the films. One such quest sees either Jason or Lucia held at gunpoint by a stand-in for Tom Cruise’s character from Collateral. If you want to trigger this event and get out alive, make sure to read on!

This encounter is a standout, not appearing anywhere on the map and not being accessible until midway into Chapter 3. Once you’ve gained easy access to Vice City and start heading toward Vice Beach, sitting in any car alone for an extended period gives a suited stranger a chance to enter the back seat suddenly.

He’ll proceed to stick up the protagonist, forcing them to start driving. From here on, failure to comply with his orders will lead to him shooting the player, not enough to kill outright, but enough to push you over the edge if you’re already wounded.

Your next task is to run a red light, any red light you can find. Thankfully, the agent is rather patient as long as he can tell you’re looking for a light or waiting for one to change. Once it’s clear you can follow instructions, he’ll mark an area near the park in Vice Beach for you to drive to, a trek depending on where you started the mission.

Make sure you don’t slow down too much or try to turn on the radio. Your passenger wants a nice, quiet ride to his destination. Once you arrive, things change fast, giving you a split-second decision.

Once you arrive at the location, the agent will explain that this entire charade was to put the protagonist’s face and car on a police suspect database for running that red light. Now that you’ve made it to his destination, we’re about to be in real hot water, as he guns down a nearby guard protecting a small drug lab.

He insists you leave, but if you’re feeling spiteful or profit-focused, you can easily follow him inside. Without a gun to your head, he’s as easy to take down as any other enemy, plus he’ll have already cleared the guards inside and outside the lab.

Make sure to keep your car running by double-tapping your exit button, and quickly pocket everything he stood to gain before heading out. He wasn’t kidding, the cops are already on their way, so whether you’re willing to snag some for yourself or just want to hightail it, make sure you leave fast.

I’d fully recommend hitting the lab, as it’s easily a 10k payout for very little effort. There are also a few handy guns to pocket if you need the hardware. The Jeep parked outside sells for a pretty penny as well, giving you an excuse to swing by Randy and continue his questline.

#4107. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

#4106. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

#4104. 10 Best Food Centric Video Games

Eric Warner is a Journalist and Multimedia Producer based in New England with over 7 years of experience producing stories for multiple publications

For many countries across the globe, 2026’s holiday season is just around the corner. With those holidays come celebratory family gatherings full of all kinds of delicious food to eat.

While some people may be stressing out about the prospect of cooking so many dishes for the holiday season, there’s likely just as many people out there who not only enjoy tasting all kinds of meals but enjoy preparing them for friends and family alike as well.

For those who love cooking and all things food-related, here’s a look at the 10 best food centric video games people can enjoy playing through, whether solo or with friends, in between tantalizing holiday meals.

For a few decades now, food companies have occasionally released tie-in video games often referred to as advergames, in wacky attempts to attract gamers to purchase their products. While Burger King has released a few advergames over the years, its best was arguably Sneak King.

One of three BK games for the original Xbox and Xbox 360, Sneak King is a third-person stealth game following the fast-food chain’s now-retired Burger King mascot, as he sneaks around various locations to surprise deliver BK meals such as omelet sandwiches, hash browns, and more.

While Sneak King didn’t have a lot of depth to it, the game did represent the often wacky yet creative game design the sixth and seventh console generations are remembered for.

Anybody who grew up owning an iPod Touch, iPad, or iPhone in the early 2010s likely played some of the most iconic mobile apps of all time, such as Angry Birds, Doodle Jump, and the subject for this entry, Halfbrick Studios’ Fruit Ninja.

The premise for Fruit Ninja is simple: players must use a touch screen, VR controllers, or their own hands (in the case of the Kinect versions) to equip ninja blades and slice up as much flying fruit as possible without hitting flying bombs.

Fruit Ninja is an easy game for sure, but it’s one that endlessly fun no matter what form or mode it’s played in, whether it be the Xbox 360 Kinect version, the Fruit Ninja FX version found at Dave & Buster's and other arcades, or the latest version on Nex Playground.

J. R. R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings franchise is beloved for many reasons, such as its mythology, character arcs, and fantastical creatures. Another aspect of the franchise many people adore is the calm, joyful culture of Hobbit life.

Numerous LOTR fans strive to live life as merrily as the Shire’s inhabitants, and one way people can do so is by playing the life simulation game Tales of the Shire: A The Lord of the Rings Game, set after The Hobbit but before The Fellowship of the Ring.

Here, players can create their own Hobbit as they complete tasks such as farming, fishing, and decorating Hobbit-holes in the emerging Hobbiton village of Bywater. Most importantly for this article, they can also cook a variety of dishes for their Hobbit neighbors.

In this preview, let's discuss KuloNiku: Bowl Up! A game that feels like a soft spiritual successor to the Papa Louie cooking titles at its heart.

In 2006, Nintendo helped many young gamers get interested in cooking for the first time by releasing the minigame compilation Cooking Mama on the Nintendo DS. While that game is fantastic, many Nintendo players would consider Cooking Mama 5: Bon Appétit! to be the best entry in the CM series.

The final mainline entry in the CM series, Cooking Mama 5: Bon Appétit! Features similar modes and overall gameplay to its predecessors, but introduces many new minigames and recipes such as Pumpkin Gratin, Hawaiian Pancakes, and Herb Hotdogs.

Players could even manage a burger shop, take care of pet fish, customize kitchen designs, and gather ingredients from plants, with each action feeling more precise thanks to the 3DS’ improved stylus controls.

Video games have let people play as medieval heroes, monsters, space marines, and more, but one unique game did the impossible by making playing as actual food fun. That game was Bossa Studios’ I Am Bread.

Set in the same universe as Surgeon Simulator, I Am Bread has players control a singular piece of bread as it strives to move about various locations such as a kitchen and a bathroom in an effort to become toast, whilst struggling to maintain its edibility by avoiding the ground, bugs, and other contaminants.

While the premise of I Am Bread might sound ridiculous at first, it actually winds up being a fairly hilarious, challenging, and rewarding game, with all of the crazy antics and chaos the slices of bread get into.

People love parties, candy, and piñatas, but only one game developer has dared tackling the question of how piñatas are made. As seen in Rare’s classic life simulation game Viva Piñata.

Set on the initially ruinous Pinata island, Viva Piñata has players restore a garden on the island with the goal of attracting, domesticating, breeding, and defending local piñata wildlife, so that they can eventually be sent out to parties across the globe full of delicious candy.

Viva Piñata may be 20 years old at this point, but it’s still just as fun and colorful as ever, whether people play it on Xbox 360, PC, or via the Rare Replay compilation.

Hunger meters aren’t a law of nature. These ten survival games turned food into a reward, made it optional or ditched eating altogether.

The Illinois-based game developer Young Horses is famous for its Octodad series, which itself could be considered a food centric game since a chef chases Octodad around. However, the team wound up making one of the most creative food centric games yet in 2020, with Bugsnax.

Here, people play as a muppet-like Grumpus newspaper journalist, as they set out to Snaktooth Island to document the food-like Bugsnax creatures living there only to get caught up in a mysterious conspiracy surrounding the island and its inhabitants.

For anyone who wanted to explore the living food island of Swallow Falls in Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2, Bugsnax is the game for you. You can encounter all kinds of food-inspired wildlife on Snaktooth Island, such as the elephant cheeseburger Bunger and the crab apple Crapple.

Many of the best food centric games were released years or even decades ago, but one new 2026 title has quickly become a favorite among food fanatics. That game being the anime-inspired cooking and restaurant management simulator KuloNiku: Bowl Up!

The 13th game released by Gambir Studio, KuloNiku: Bowl Up! has players inherit their grandmother’s once-famous meatball restaurant in the cozy town of KuloNiku. They set out to restore it to its former glory by experimenting with new recipes, decor, and competing with other chefs in Meatball Brawls.

People aren’t just making simple spaghetti and meatball dishes, though, as customers will often request comedically complex recipes requiring players to chop, boil, fry, and torch all kinds of ingredients, with some customers even going on to become potential friends or rivals.

Conquer the depths of a dark dungeon as you craft delicious new recipies.

Many food centric games focus on people opening up a new restaurant and rising to Michelin star status, but no game quite replicates that experience in such a unique and fun way like Mintrocket’s Dave the Diver.

A primarily 2D adventure and management game, Dave the Diver follows the title character as he and his friends open their Bancho Sushi Bar near a massive, mysterious Blue Hole, with Dave having to dive for fish during the day and manage the sushi restaurant at night.

Diving for fish and managing the sushi restaurant are certainly fun activities, but there's far more to Dave the Diver than initially meets the eye. Players can fight huge sea creature bosses, sing karaoke, and even interact with mermaids from the Sea People Village.

Without a doubt, the best food centric game out there is Ghost Town Games’ Overcooked! All You Can Eat, a remastered collection of Overcooked and Overcooked 2 with all DLC expansions and completely brand-new content.

A third-person, top-down perspective cooking game, Overcooked 1 and 2 feature teams of up to four chefs working together to serve food in an orderly, oftentimes hectic, manner from restaurants, food trucks, and unconventional locations such as a space station and icebergs.

While Overcooked may not be as realistic with its food as other games, it perfectly recreates the fun, often chaotic nature of restaurant cooking into a cartoony, co-op experience and forces people to learn to work together as a team, making it a perfect food centric game.

Greg has more than than 10 years of experience in video game journalism, covering some of the biggest games on the 8th and 9th generations of console.

Just days after Grand Theft Auto 6’s massive November 19 launch, a PlayStation player has found themselves in hot water after sharing a NSFW image from the game with a PSN friend.

Player derickgott007 shared his experience on X (via TweakTown) that he received a 30-day ban from PlayStation’s social features after sharing a photo from GTA 6’s infamous nudist resort, leading him to put out a strong warning on social media.

A bug that causes crashes has cropped up for PS5 players of Grand Theft Auto 6, forcing them to close the game for no apparent reason.

While the offending image was not shared, GTA 6’s nudist areas feature a mix of fully clothed and naked NPCs roaming around, mirroring the real experiences of clothing-optional resorts that are a roaring trade in coastal Florida. The image was sent via PSN’s private message service and not posted publicly on any part of Sony’s gaming service.

Although the photo was taken with GTA 6’s in-game camera application and did not feature real-world nudity, PlayStation somehow flagged the image as pornographic and sent a message saying it breached the service’s Code of Conduct. The game’s hyper-realistic graphics might have tricked Sony’s strict auto-moderation tools that real sensitive images were being sent.

The game’s hyper-realistic graphics might have tricked Sony’s strict auto-moderation tools that real sensitive images were being sent.

The player was warned that any further infractions could lead to permanent suspension, causing him to frantically post on social media about his experience.

In their post, the player cautioned others: "Do not, I repeat, do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity." The official notice from PlayStation Safety confirmed the content "breached the Code of Conduct" and cited "pornographic or obscene content."

The ban comes as a real risk for players who share content from the game online, meaning auto-moderation tools on social media or messaging services may inadvertently restrict content featuring risque or outright obscene imagery.

While PSN flagged pornographic content, the irony comes that Sony is actively promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 on a grand scale across its platform, featuring multiple ads and promotional images that encourage players to pick the game up on PlayStation.

However, Sony also has to abide with the local laws of the hundreds of countries it operates in, meaning that its auto-moderation tools must respond quickly to perceived threats or the breaking of rules to protect young and vulnerable customers from harm. The company does not grant exceptions, even for unedited screenshots captured from M-rated games sold directly through its own storefront.

Sony also has to abide with the local laws of the hundreds of countries it operates in, meaning that its auto-moderation tools must respond quickly to perceived threats.

The response has been mixed, with netizens online commenting that the ban is disproportionately harsh considering the image came from a game being actively pushed by Sony. Others argued that rules are rules, and that perhaps instead of a ban, Sony should simply block the offending content to prevent it being seen by the receiving party.

One user even urged derickgott07 to sue Sony in a class action lawsuit, saying the company “wouldn’t have a leg to stand on” and that it broke its own Code of Conduct by selling a sexually explicit game on its own marketplace. Figure that one out.

GTA 6 is on track to be one of the biggest games of all time, but developers at Rockstar Games still have worries about job security.

#4102. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it launched, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating currently sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

#4100. Best Netflix games available right now - From Into the Breach to Red Dead Redemption

Netflix isn't just a place to watch movies and TV episodes - it's also a great place for gamers to discover new forms of entertainment, with a large library of games from many different developers and genres.

There are numerous hours of fun to be had on Netflix for gamers, from action to puzzle games. On the next pages, you can find a list we compiled after carefully considering all the available games and narrowing them down to give you the top 10 best Netflix games at the moment. How to find and install Netflix Games If you don't have it already, go ahead and download the Netflix app on your device. Keep in mind that you need to have an active Netflix subscription for this.

Now, let's get on with the list of best Netflix games at the moment.

If you don't know anything about the Football Manager franchise, you must be either living under a rock or you just don't like football. But if you do like football and simulation games, then this is a no-brainer.

Become a club manager and take everything under your control, from tactics and transfers to team talks, scouting, and pretty much anything else that you can imagine.

You can start your career at any club in the world, as it supports every league and has real players. As I said, this game is a must if you are looking for a football simulation experience.

Download now! Football Manager 26 Mobile

You already know about Bloons TD 6 from our previous articles, such as Bloons TD 6 tier list and best towers to carry your rounds. In this Netflix game, you benefit from hundreds of configurations and upgrades, so feel free to read all the guides we've created to help you on that journey.

Aside from that, what you need to know about this game is that it's wild. You have a tower defence type of game where things get increasingly more difficult. Towards the last levels, some players even reported crashes because of how crazy the battles turned out.

It's one of the most fun and entertaining tower defence games out there, and easily one of the best games Netflix has to offer.

Oxenfree is a story-driven adventure game with elements of mystery and suspense, sprinkled with paranormal elements.

The story follows a group of teenagers as they face the repercussions of opening a ghostly portal on an abandoned island, while out partying one night. It's also got a smart chat system that lets players have a major impact on the tale's action and conclusion.

New graphics, a remixed soundtrack, a new epilogue, mysteries, and branching story paths can all be found in Oxenfree: Netflix Edition, which was published on September 24th, 2022. If you are interested in this title, here's a link to our full review of Oxenfree, where we get into specifics.

Before Your Eyes is a game with a major focus on storytelling and beauty. The actual story is a little dark at its core, but the way it is presented is far from it.

It gives players the opportunity to immerse themselves in an individual's life, as they journey across the River Styx and into the afterlife. That is as dark as it appears, but it has its beauty.

Before Your Eyes has innovative gameplay with real-time tracking of the player's eye movements and blinking to make choices that impact the outcome of the story. It's not something we typically see in your run-of-the-mill mobile game.

Krispee Street is an adorably designed hidden object game that is exclusively accessible to Netflix members. This title draws inspiration from a well-known webcomic, and its graphics don't shy away from showing that. It's really well done.

As a player, you'll have to figure out puzzles and discover well-hidden objects, and while it might sound like a piece of cake at first, it really isn't. Oh, and it also has a certain narrative that it manages to tell between the puzzles and hidden object games. It's really good, and a nice break from the classical, realistic hidden object game we're used to.

As a kid, you've probably dreamed of defending the Earth from various calamities or invasions and being a hero in the end. Well, Into the Breach will make your childhood dream finally come true. You're the last line of defence against the overgrown bug-like aliens that can crush a building without much effort. However, humanity has advanced, and we have huge mechs and other weapons of destruction because we humans are great at finding the best way to kill each other.

Fighting is done on an 8x8 grid that's similar to chess, with turn-based combat. As terrain can shift and create huge holes in the ground, it can be tricky to avoid them while facing aliens. Therefore, careful planning is essential to win every round, no matter what the end goal is. That's the only way to turn terrain shifts to your advantage, as gravity works on your adversaries as well.

Storyteller is a hit game unlike any other. It starts off pretty slow, with just a couple of prompts, but soon enough you will find yourself in a story unlike any other. The game is available on Steam as well, which is where it was first popularised.

The best part about Storyteller is not the fact that it's sort of a build-your-own-story kind of game, but rather its unique take on it. You will be in charge of making a plot for each prompt you're given, and sometimes these plots have a twist. Literally. It's one of the best Netflix games ever released, and you shouldn't skip it.

Red Dead Redemption likely needs no introduction, though we should take a moment to appreciate how far mobile has come before we get to that. The fact that we can now carry an incredibly complex and detailed open-world shooter like this in our pockets shows the leaps in technology since the game first released way back in 2010.

If you're somehow unfamiliar, it takes place in the Wild West and follows John Marston as he hunts down the surviving members of his old gang. Why? The federal government has taken his family and won't give them back until the job is done. Yeah, it's pretty heavy stuff and is a wonderfully told story. In some ways, I'd argue, it's better than its successor, Red Dead 2. I appreciate that’s a contentious statement, of course.

But it's not all gloomy stuff. Thanks to the open-world nature of it all, there's plenty of twisted fun to be had with tying people to train tracks and waiting for the next locomotive to roll through. Or if you don’t want to act like a Looney Tunes villain, you can swagger into a saloon, find a comfortable corner, and play poker for hours instead. It’s good fun either way.

Download now! Red Dead Redemption NETFLIX

Death might not be the happiest topic in the world, but that doesn't mean it can't provide some level of catharsis when handled well. Spiritfarer takes this complex life event and somehow manages to turn it into a cosy management RPG.

You play as a ferrymaster tasked with guiding the recently passed to the afterlife. It's not a simple case of starting the engines and sailing across to the other side, though. The spirits you encounter are somewhat restless, and you'll need to care for them as they make their final voyage. That means getting to know them and their needs, which makes for an incredibly emotional final goodbye. Still, it's that bittersweet variety of sadness where you'll be pleased you took the plunge.

Aside from chatting to Spiritfarer's lovable cast, you'll also busy yourself with fishing, crafting, mining, farming, and all manner of other things. Just because your destination is a fairly morbid one, it doesn't mean that everyday tasks can fall by the wayside, you see. They're still important and in many ways key to the relaxing vibe Spiritfarer offers.

I've had fairly mixed opinions about Black Mirror ever since it jumped to Netflix. Though there have been plenty of good episodes since that move (Hi, San Junipero), I mostly find the quality has dipped (What was that awful werewolf episode all about?). However, Season 6's Plaything does stand out as one of the better offerings from the later series.

Now, that could simply be because my opinion is swayed by the video game stuff or the fantastic performance from Peter Capaldi (The best Doctor Who since the show's revival. Sorry, David). But either way, the fictional video game featured in it isn't actually fictional. Sort of. That's right, you can actually play Thronglets! It's just these little critters don't plan to kill us all... I think.

Inspired by Black Mirror mastermind Charlie Brooker's obsession with keeping a Tamagotchi alive in his youth, Thronglets is a virtual pet sim that tasks you with helping the Throng thrive. They'll hatch from eggs before relying on you for food and entertainment. Do all those things, and you'll have an adorable little army (?). Just don't set them all on fire, alright? They don't take too kindly to that.

One Zelda fan just reminded everyone we never really forget their trickshot skills.

The power of the OcarinaVR mod is quite the sight to behold. It goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective with accurate spatial scaling—meaning the world adjusts depending on whether the player is controlling young Link or the grown-up version.

The mod also brings intricate control mechanics and hand tracking, allowing players to map and control Link’s arms and individual fingers using their VR controllers. Swinging the Master sword and bashing enemies with the Hylian shield never looks so satisfying and adds a sense of depth and realism to the game beyond just its graphics.

OcarinaVR also manages UI elements and prevents clutter, displaying HUD readouts like heart count and the minimap as floating panels. Pre-rendered cutscenes are displayed on a curved virtual cinema screen for maximum immersion as the perspective shifts back to the 3rd person.

OcarinaVR … goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective.

The mod is based on the Hookshot PC recompilation that was released on PC shortly after Ocarina of Time launched on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5. That release already brought native widescreen and uncapped framerates, meaning it was a solid foundation for the OcarinaVR mod to build off.

Fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental, with players praising its highly-detailed graphics and faithful retelling of the classic Zelda tale. Critics loved it equally as much, giving it one of the highest ratings on Metacritic of all time—a solid 95/100 aggregated score.

In DualShockers’ own review, Tayna Garcia wrote that the remake gives returning players an “opportunity to experience those same feelings again” from their childhoods, powered by nostalgia, but said it's a perfect place for newcomers to start their Zelda journey, too.

Fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental [and] critics loved it equally as much.

The game was swiftly followed by Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6—perhaps the most hyped game of all time (and the highest reviewed on Metacritic with a stunning score of 99). Nintendo knew to get Zelda out the door before the news cycle and social media turned to GTA 6 for who knows how long.

The new VR mod gives fans a chance to take on Ocarina of Time in a whole new way, snatching a little bit of attention back from the Vice City-drenched mediascape right now.

Some of the original's most charming quirks from Zelda: Ocarina of Time didn't make the journey.

#4098. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.
