#4071. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 13, 2026

Today is Friday the 13th, but let's not dwell on that. Here are some weekend video games to play. Well, actually, here are some of our biggest stories of the week, and then you can check out some weekend game recommendations.

Also, go ahead and make some space on your Xbox or PlayStation hard drive to make room for GTAVI. It's going to be about 200 GB and you can pre-load it now. Delete those games you're not going to return to. Delete all those video clips you'll never watch from every time you get a Trophy on your PlayStation. And you know what? Go ahead and delete Fortnite, too. It's time.

Calling all sickos of The Rootrees Are Dead, Return of the Obra Dinn, The Incident At Galley House, and everything in between: there’s another good deduction game to obsess over. Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.

NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.

Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.

Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.

It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.

Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.

You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.

As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on current platforms with modernized improvements to boot.

If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.

I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.

FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.

Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.

If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

#4070. GTA 6 Hacker Walks Free Despite Seven-Year Sentence, Just Days After Launch

The hacker behind GTA 6's massive 2022 leak was sentenced to seven years in prison on November 23. But instead of returning to prison, Arion Kurtaj walked out of Woolwich Crown Court that day, just four days after Rockstar's long-awaited game launched.

The person who leaked more than 90 Grand Theft Auto 6 production videos seems to be trying to reach an agreement with Rockstar Games

As Dexerto reports, the 21-year-old was released on licence after the court took account of the time he'd already spent in custody. He's also subject to a five-year order limiting what he can do online. So while the sentence sounds surprising, his release doesn't mean the charges were dropped.

Kurtaj was part of the Lapsus$ hacking group and had been detained for years while his case worked its way through the courts. In December 2023, he was placed in a secure hospital after being deemed unfit to stand trial. A later assessment found him fit to plead, and he was moved to prison in January 2026.

On November 16, he pleaded guilty to a series of offences connected to cyberattacks on Rockstar Games and other companies. DualShockers covered his guilty plea at the time, noting how close it was to GTA 6's November 19 release. His sentencing followed exactly one week later.

Kurtaj had already spent enough time in custody to be released on licence rather than sent back to prison. Walking out of court doesn't mean he can go straight back to his old online life.

He's now subject to a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting his online activity, including a ban on using Discord and Telegram. It's a significant condition for someone who committed cyberattacks while already on bail.

Walking out of court doesn't mean he can go straight back to his old online life.

Justice Turner also warned Kurtaj about wasting his abilities on further offences. The judge described him as talented and urged him not to spend his life repeatedly returning to prison.

The case also involved attacks on Uber, Revolut, and BT/EE. According to the UK Crown Prosecution Service, Kurtaj's activities exposed sensitive information and disrupted business systems. In the BT/EE case, prosecutors linked his intrusion to unauthorized SIM swaps, which could let criminals take over other people's calls and messages. He also admitted to possessing a mobile phone in prison, an offence dating to March 2026.

Back in September 2022, Kurtaj obtained 90 GTA 6 gameplay videos from Rockstar's systems and posted the footage online under the name TeaPotUberHacker. It gave everyone an early, unfinished look at the next Grand Theft Auto, long before Rockstar was ready to show it off. Rockstar sources reportedly confirmed the footage was genuine shortly afterwards.

One of the stranger details is how he did it. Kurtaj was already on bail for other cybercrimes and had been moved to a hotel for his own protection. From there, he used a phone, the hotel's television Wi-Fi, and an Amazon Fire Stick to carry out further attacks, including the one on Rockstar.

The leaked footage showed parts of Vice City and early gameplay involving the game's two leads. Kurtaj also tried to blackmail Rockstar by threatening to release the game's source code unless the company contacted him. The 90 videos were released; the source code was what he threatened to put out next.

The damage wasn't just about fans seeing the game early. Rockstar reportedly spent around $5 million and thousands of staff hours dealing with the breach, according to Dexerto. That was on top of the disruption to other companies targeted in the same hacking spree.

Those clips spread across the internet more than four years before GTA 6's November 19 release. Now that the game is finally out, Kurtaj's case has reached sentencing too. He's left prison, but the online restrictions attached to his release will continue for another five years.

#4069. Ember Outpost offers the Rimworld experience on mobile, out now for iOS and Android

Space, the final frontier. And like all frontiers, there's always someone willing to take a chance on building a new life there, no matter how much of a ludicrously ill-advised idea it may be. It's a concept that offers rich ground for colony management sims, but there haven't been many options for that on mobile, well, until Ember Outpost arrived.

Available now on iOS and Android, Ember Outpost is a colony management sim that sees you guiding a group of settlers on an alien world. Everything, from food to water and other supplies, will need to be crafted or collected, and you'll also have to deal with the drastically contradictory personalities of your colonists. Oh, and let's add natural disasters and murderous raiders, just for some extra spice.

It's not all sunshine and roses, though. Ember Outpost does have the lingering spectre of AI in some bizarrely high-res assets scattered throughout, and promotional imagery. Which is a shame because I think part of the appeal of colony sims such as RimWorld is how easily readable and minimalist they are. But you can't have everything.

For what it is, Ember Outpost offers exactly what those who want RimWorld on mobile have been waiting for. Densely detailed colony sim action, where there's just as much potential for disasters inside the walls of your compound as outside of it.

If you think you might like to practice a little before taking your foray into the great unknown, then why not check out some of our choice picks of the best strategy games on Android?

#4068. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4066. Gunboat God offers blazingly fast, inky black bullet hell action for you on iOS and Android

Nowadays, with the popularity of Vampire Survivors, it seems as though the humble bullet hell has become somewhat passe in the face of the bullet heaven. But Gunboat God, now available on iOS and Android, may just prove that the bullet hell genre isn't dead by a long shot!

Gunboat God is an inky black-and-white take on the bullet hell and shoot-em-up genre, where your only aim is to slay as many enemies as possible and make your way back to the Citadel in the sky. Gunboat God is blisteringly fast-paced, exciting and difficult, but rewardingly so. Either way you certainly won't be forgetting this distinctive mashup of platformer, bullet hell and run 'n gun anytime soon!

#4065. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

#4064. 8 Best Connections to GTA 5 in GTA 6

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Rockstar spent a long time working on Grand Theft Auto 6, and it shows through the games many small details. There are tons of hidden easter eggs and secrets scattered across Leonida, and some of them connect to previous GTA titles.

More specifically, there are a decent number that connect back to GTA 5. Have you ever wondered what happened to Michael’s boat? Who took the blame for the murder of Floyd and Debora?

Thanks to GTA 6, we now the answers to these questions, and there are many more connections to GTA 5 that you might not have discovered. Everything is connected after all.

If you played GTA 5, odds are you spent a great deal of time exploring the map and going from town to town. It was quite a big map, but you wouldn’t have spent your entire time in the city, so you probably recognize Grapeseed and the Grand Senora Desert.

Grapeseed is a small town in the northern part of the GTA 5 map, with it residing in Blaine County. The Grand Senora Desert is a much larger area, but it also resides in Blaine County.

While exploring the many buildings that you can enter in GTA 6, you can wander into a few trailers, and some of them have postcards that link Leonida to Los Santos. You can find postcards specifically for Grapeseed and Grand Senora Desert.

You get a lot of phone calls in GTA 5. Many missions start with you getting a call, and then proceeding to head to some location. Because of this, if you have played the story, you will have heard Michael’s ringtone quite a bit.

Well, if you feel so inclined, and want to stay true to the spirit of GTA 5, you can have Michael’s ringtone in GTA 6. All you need to do is go into your phone’s settings, choose the ringtone option, and then select the one called Wind Chimes.

This ringtone is exactly the same as Michael’s from GTA 5, giving you that classic GTA feeling from 13 years ago when you played the campaign for GTA 5.

With the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, it is time to look back and remind ourselves why Grand Theft Auto 5 will be remember for years to come.

One of the best easter eggs in GTA 6 is that you can find Michael’s boat from GTA 5, and you don’t really need to go all that far. In fact, you have to stick rather close to home, because it is sitting right outside Jason’s house at the start of the game.

Michael ends up having his boat stolen in GTA 5, and you never learn what happens to it. Well, it somehow found its way to Leonida and ended up in Jason’s yard.

If you decide to climb up on the boat, you can see that a screen is still active on it. This screen shows the shores of Los Santos from GTA 5, seemingly proving that this is indeed the same boat that was stolen from Michael all those years ago.

Do you remember Fabien? He teaches Michael how to do yoga in GTA 5, and is known for having some rather… suggestive yoga poses. Throughout GTA 5, you can perform yoga as Michael either at his house or at the peak of Mount Gordo.

Fabien has been doing well since the events of GTA 5, and you can see what he has been up to thanks to his article in one of the game’s magazines. This is also an easter egg that you can find outside of Jason’s house.

Go out onto the porch, and open the magazine that is on the table near the workout equipment. Flip through the pages, and you will find that Fabien has been doing well. He has been on an “epic pilgrimage of enlightenment.”

It is a little ambiguous as to if the Mount Chiliad Mystery in GTA 5 was ever solved. While there is a means of seeing a UFO from it, it didn’t have a narrative conclusion, so it is debated on whether or not it was ever completed.

However, this mystery is mentioned in GTA 6, and it is on a vehicle. You can find an RV in Leonida that is covered in phrases like, “Don’t be fooled,” and “There’s no driving away.”

What connects this to Mount Chiliad is the eye symbol. It is the same eye symbol that is found at the top of the Mount Chiliad mural, making it seem like the mystery was never fully solved, or maybe that is just what Rockstar wants us to think.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a nominee for Game of the Year. It was selected at the last minute, but there are plenty of reasons it deserves the award.

There are some small nods to GTA 5 hidden throughout GTA 6, and one that is easy to overlook is a small book review for a novel sitting in Jason’s house. The book in question is titled Lethal By Design: A Liberty City Memoir, written by Tom Everett.

This book connects to the events of GTA 4 and Niko Bellic - a fan-favorite protagonist. With that being said, one of the reviews is actually from a resident of Los Santos.

The review reads, “Illuminating, revelatory, heartbreaking, and pulse-quickening - and that’s before you’ve even finished the editor’s forward.” This review came from Alison Taylor from the Los Santos Book Review.

There is an obscure reference to GTA 5 in GTA 6, and it connects back to some of the promotional material for GTA 5. One of the trailers for GTA 5 featured a man with a newspaper on his desk.

If you are paying attention, you can see that the newspaper’s headline reads, “Aliens ate my prize [blank]. Of course, I have to bleep out the final word due to vulgarity, but it connected to GTA 4, and it also played into the insane satirical nature of GTA 5.

This same newspaper has returned, and it is in GTA 6. In a shack in the Grassrivers, you can spot the same newspaper sitting on a table. It is amazing that Rockstar remembered to bring back this strange newspaper.

Floyd and Debora Hebert were an unhappy couple living in Vespucci Beach in GTA 5. Their house is used as a safehouse by Trevor and their cousin Wade. However, they don’t survive the events of GTA 5, as Trevor murders them in a brutal off-screen killing that leaves him covered in blood.

It is never known exactly what happened after that event, but you can learn the truth of what transpired after the events of GTA 5 by listening to the radio in GTA 6.

If you listen to the crime thriller podcast channel on the radio, you will hear them talk about Floyd and Debora. It turns out that Wade got blamed for their deaths.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4063. Sakurai Celebrates Kirby Air Riders' First Anniversary And Seemingly Ponders His Future As A Game Creator

He's apparently still working at "full throttle"

As we reflect on 25 years of Super Smash Bros. Melee, it seems game director Masahiro Sakurai is taking a moment to remind everyone that Kirby Air Riders has now been available for a year.

As highlighted by Sakurai on social media, the Switch 2 exclusive is officially one year old as of this week. It's received multiple updates since launch and Nintendo recently rolled out the last two amiibo.

In the game director's message, he also touches on his future as a game creator. Here's a rough translation of this part of Sakurai's post via EventHubs: "Time flies. I wonder how much more I'll be able to make".

Sakurai admittedly isn't getting any younger, and Kirby Air Riders included "everything" at launch, so it seems this is a genuine reflection on his future as a game creator. He has reportedly claimed to be semi-retired in the past, but this eventually led to Kirby Air Riders. He's also raised his future within the game industry on multiple other occasions.

Just earlier this week at the Famitsu 40th Anniversary Festival, Sakurai apparently revisited a column he had written about retirement, and how his decision depends on the demand for his work, and if he remains capable of delivering it (via OtakuKart). He's also questioned when his "spirit" might break. For now, though, he's still apparently working at "full throttle".

If we do hear any significant updates about Sakurai's future projects, or anything else he is up to, we'll be sure to let you know.

#4062. Suits & Stallions is a classy little party game that lets you race horses, now on iOS and Android

When it comes to 'classy' party games, I'd be hard-pressed to think of any. By their very nature, most party games are lighthearted and fun, but that's where Suits & Stallions comes in: a new entry in the genre available now on iOS and Android that leans into the classier side of the equation.

What's the classiest thing you can imagine? Horse racing, of course! And that's what Suits & Stallions is all about, as you race your porcelain model horses across a board in a classily lit museum setting. Each card you draw can move either you, your opponent or both, depending on the corresponding suit, but you can try to nudge the results or whip your chosen stallion into shape for a better chance at success.

There are also other optional modes, such as Troika, which sees you racing an entire tower of horses rather than one. And the best part is that if you stay playing against the PC, then all of this is free!

Of course, the main appeal of any party game is playing with your friends, and in that regard Suits & Stallions is an interesting example of the genre. Less likely to cause pure chaos, but I can see a devious card draw and decision to send your friend back causing plenty of lighthearted arguments.

You can find Suits & Stallions right now on iOS and Android. But if you're looking for even more free-to-play games, then mobile is definitely the place to be. Just take a look at our list of the best free mobile games of 2026 for some of our choice picks!

#4060. Affordable Gaming Dream Dies as Nvidia Reinstates AI-First CEO

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Earlier this very month, Jensen Huang, CEO of the world’s leading chip producer, Nvidia, not to mention one of the most crucial companies to the advancement of gaming as a creator of GPUs, was wracked with controversy. Huang admitted an affair with a woman alleged to be a spy for the Chinese government and was also accused of an affair with an Nvidia executive, according to the BBC.

Following all of these revelations, Huang voluntarily resigned from his position as CEO. For a brief, glorious moment, the gaming community breathed a sigh of relief, as it was Huang’s gung-ho attitude on AI-centric developments over all else that had largely contributed to Nvidia shifting focus away from gaming hardware. Maybe we’d start seeing affordable, optimized GPUs again!

Unfortunately, we are not allowed to have nice things in this timeline. According to a BBC report this morning, following a unanimous vote from the current Nvidia corporate board, Huang has been officially reinstated to his position as CEO. Yay.

Microsoft has filed a brand new patent for swappable XBOX controller thumbsticks as a new alternative for stick drift and other forms of damage.

According to the BBC report, despite previous insistences from the board that Huang would not be reinstated to his position, the ultimate conclusion that they came to is that only Huang could continue the AI-focused push Nvidia has been running with lately.

"The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," the board’s current chair said in a public statement on the Nvidia website.

The ultimate conclusion that they came to is that only Huang could continue the AI-focused push Nvidia has been running with lately.

Apparently, Huang’s return was orchestrated at least in part by United States President Donald Trump, who, in a brief interview with CNBC, said that he “felt very strongly that [Huang] should come back, and we've done a very thorough investigation.

"And the investigation showed that he did - I mean, he had bad judgment having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents - but he did nothing wrong other than he created a chip that's invaluable."

Following news of Huang’s reinstatement, Nvidia’s stock value bounced up 32%, a notable increase following a 13% drop-off at the end of last week.

In a personal statement on the Nvidia website, Huang said that he is “honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”

Some analysts speculate that, particularly within the AI-centric tech field, figureheads have become an important part of the push. Parallels have been drawn between Huang’s reinstatement and that of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who was reinstated in his own position just five days after being fired from it in 2023.

The BBC’s tech and AI analyst Zoe Kleinman posited on the matter, saying that “It says a lot that despite the serious accusations made about him and his affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy, ultimately his position in the tech industry has proved to be more important:

“There had been many calls for him to be reinstated - including from within the UK House of Lords - on the grounds that the AI industry would be weaker without him.”

Whatever the precise reason, it’s probably a safe bet that Nvidia will promptly resume its previous course, which means those of us in the gaming sphere won’t be seeing any affordable GPUs any time soon. Oh well, it was nice to dream of a world where you didn't need to justify buying a top-shelf graphics card...

Downing Street is celebrating Rockstar's latest blockbuster as a major British achievement, but don't expect Prime Minister Andy Burnham to join the millions of players exploring Vice City.

#4059. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

If any of that sounds interesting, definitely log in now to play the pre-launch event, which should hold you over until the proper show kicks off Saturday. If you’re already enjoying Heartopia, you likely want to learn about Onsen Egg Promise locations, Fish locations, and Bug locations - all of which can be found at those links.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

Sacrilicious Treats Heartopia Wonder Egg Hunt: All egg locations

Wild At Heart Heartopia animal food: All trough locations and each animal's favourite foods

The Way To A Heart Heartopia Cooking recipes: How to obtain every recipe and variant

#4055. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (21st November)

Pretty quiet week in the world of video games, eh? Nothing particularly groundbreaking released that we can think of...

Oh wait! Yes, that Grand Theft Auto 6 launched, didn't it? And it was a rather big deal. The game shot to the top of Metacritic's all-time best games list (tied with the original Ocarina of Time), and Digital Foundry weighed in on whether it'll ever come to Switch 2.

On a more Nintendo-related note, the Wii celebrated its 20th anniversary, Nintendo was named the most-nominated publisher at this year's The Game Awards, and a brand-new event got underway in Pokémon Pokopia.

All of this meant that it was a slightly quieter one in review land, but we still shared our thoughts on TANUKI: Pon's Summer (7/10).

Feature 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can

Talking Point As A Parent, What Worries You Most About Gaming?

Nintendo's guide aims to highlight the benefits

So, is anyone playing something other than GTA this weekend?

I wrapped up Ocarina this week, and after a few days of feeling like an empty shell of a man (that ending still rips), I've been back to my backlog in an attempt to clear some before the year is up.

It's been Well Dweller that has been gobbling up most of my time. I think I'm about halfway through now, and it really is delightful. Hopefully I'll make a bit more progress with that this weekend, and maybe finally dip my toe into Pragmata too. Who has time for GTA, eh?

I’ve been absolutely barrelling through Ocarina with the kids, ticking off the Forest, Water, Spirit, and Fire Temples (in that order - a first for me!) in quick succession. A playthrough of the original over the summer definitely helped, so we’re one temple away from the big G, with about 70 Skulltulas bagged and five heart slots left to fill.

Beyond that, Queen’s Domain has me in its grasp, and I’ve also dipped into Well Dweller. Leonida is waiting to be explored on another console, too. Video games, huh? They’re per-ritty good. Have a good one, folks.

To many people’s surprise, I joined the GTA VI bandwagon late last night and was only able to play for an hour. So I’ll likely be following Vice City traffic laws like the previous games and be an upstanding citizen.

I’m also planning on getting some more OOT time in with my main save, getting collectables so I can finally start my “Mai-ster Mode” run. I have a pretty busy weekend regardless, so I hope I can get some gaming sessions in!

I am up to mission 65 in Earth Defense Force 5, and the game continues to throw new enemies (and weapons) my way! Finally, Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 dropped on the eShop, but I must not neglect my The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time progress while serving the Emperor (surely no heresy here). I will also spend this Saturday at Lisboa Games Week, our annual video game celebration expo, and catch up with old friends while making new ones, playing fancy new and upcoming games.

My game of the week is Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader. With the GameCube’s recent 25th American release anniversary, this incredible 2001 slice of Star Wars spaceship combat action turned a quarter of a century. I am still waiting for something that surpasses it. Time to chase those secret hidden upgrades and try to go for those gold medals again. Should be “fun” in my old age and diminishing reflexes. I will have to trust the Force on this one...

Those are our plans, but what about yours? Let us know what you'll be slapping in your Switch (2) in the poll below.

That means I can finally start The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which I received on release day but held off playing until I’d finished Pipistrello. I’ve played it a few times and expect it to be as excellent as always.

Still playing Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, Theodora’s path. Thinking on going back to Divinity: Original Sin 2 before I forget what’s going on. I’m in the middle of Act 2 and need to respec the whole group as battles are a nightmare with the current setup.

GTA VI all day long. I dropped everything for this game. Thankfully, I did not listen to the crew, who said that the coolest thing ever actually sucks. I had no reason to doubt Rockstar. They always deliver, and then some. The game is even better than I could have hoped for. Jason and Lucia are great characters. It is so nice to help them get closer and deepen their love. Greetings fellow video game enthusiasts. I'm about to kick Ganondorf's door down and give him what for in Ocarina of Time. I have a fair amount of gold skulltullas and pieces of heart to find before that though. Happy gaming time everyone.

Well, another week of completely ignoring GTA VI while seemingly everyone I know has moved to Leonida. My friends have been sending me videos of themselves painting their bedrooms, furnishing their houses and texting their imaginary girlfriends, who apparently live in the same village. From what I’ve seen, the opening hours look considerably cosier than I expected. Nintendo should seriously consider suing Rockstar for shamelessly ripping off Animal Crossing.

Even my own brother attempted to get in on the action, proposing that he could “borrow” my PS5 if he bought GTA VI, promising to “return” it in a few weeks. A remarkably generous offer, I’m sure you’ll agree.

Meanwhile, back in Hyrule, I’ve been having a perfectly normal week. I found a lovely Fairy Bow and immediately began firing arrows aimlessly into paintings, solved what can only be described as a Rubik’s Cube made of green ghosts (mercifully without a timer this time), and sprinted through corridors resembling a particularly unpleasant acid trip while Navi shouted “TWISTY!” at me.

There was also the immensely satisfying moment of remembering how to dry out a rather damp room, and a light spot of sword tennis against the phantom of an old acquaintance. All in all, a productive week in the Forest Temple.

As for this weekend, I’m taking my daughter swimming for the very first time today, which I’m ridiculously excited about. Then, once we’re both suitably exhausted, I intend to venture into the Fire Temple and put that lovely complimentary red tunic to good use that a grumpy young goron insisted I take. Seems like the perfect way to warm up on a chilly autumn weekend.

Hope everyone has a wonderful weekend, whether you’re enjoying the animal crossing sim GTA6 or continuing to save Hyrule from certain doom.

My wife surprised me with GTA VI, so of course that is what I’m playing, much like the rest of the world. Similar to RDR2, I’m slowly getting a grasp on the controls and life sim mechanics. It can be a grueling process, but it will eventually become second nature.

That being said, I’ve been absolutely blown away by this game. I had been curious for years as to how Rockstar would create an open world experience better than RDR2, and I can safely say that it has been an astonishing and mind-bending.

This is a game that will have people discussing their adventures for years to come. Speaking of, I will share one of my (early) experiences.

I was driving to some rundown RV park nestled away in the middle of nowhere. As I was making my approach I saw a bloodied deer sprawled out on the rocky terrain. Once I got much closer, I see a literal Sasquatch mutilating its body. I was stunned, but I quickly hopped out of my vehicle, got my rifle, and chased after him, but to no avail.

As I make my way back to my vehicle through this thicket of bushes, muddy waters, and even some alligators, I hear gunshots in the distance. I, of course, had to investigate, and find myself stumbling upon a beat down hotel. I notice there is a door wide open, and unexpectedly hear screams. All of a sudden, there is a guy crawling on his hands and knees out of the doorway, bleeding profusely. Another scream happens.

Right there, in the hotel room, was another guy getting mauled and eaten to death by a tiger. I begin panicking as it notices me, and I begin shooting the animal multiple times before it croaks over.

Once the situation becomes calm, I ransack the hotel room. There was a flare gun, drugs, and lots of cash. Out of nowhere comes three hillbillies attempting to rob me. I quickly pull out my flare gun (on accident) and unload my ammo on these punks. They catch fire and succumb to their horrific injuries. The coast is now clear and I book it out of there.

This whole (chance) encounter was so unexpected and organic. It’s these in-between moments that solidifies Rockstar as the masters of their craft. The amount of detail and interactivity is truly awe-inspiring. I can’t wait to see what other events transpire in my next 100-hours of play.

As you probably can already tell, I'm a BIG fan of the Metroid Prime franchise, I consider it one of the best series I've ever played & one of the many very defining Nintendo giants the brand has ever brought to my gaming life.

So, inevitably, I decided to finally jump into the most recent entry of the series with Beyond and I'm absolutely loving it so far, with it being an evolution in several aspects while also not completely neglecting the core gameplay mechanics previous entries introduced to the formula. I love the little details like the visor reflecting Samus' eyes when opening the system menu, the interactivity with the world being close to what Corruption introduced with its motion controls, the emotional but impactful soundtrack & also the great visuals, especially on our 7.9 inch LCD display (I ask myself how great the game will be looking like when Nintendo will release the Switch 2 OLED model!).

Of course I can see where the frustration is coming from when players first experienced Beyond comparing it to the original series, but I also appreciate Nintendo & Retro Studios for taking a different, more cinematic & modern approach to it and I do still have the highest hopes that they will one day release the still remaining two titles of the trilogy remastered on our current day machine.

So, this is what my weekend will be looking like and as I've already said, I'm absolutely loving it. Thank you Alex for your in-depth & benevolent review on YouTube, it is greatly appreciated!

#4054. Cleanser Man Is Mega Man: Dual Override’s Boss Design Contest Winner

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.  To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

#4053. 10 Best Early Game Vehicles in GTA VI

Shane is a Contributor for DualShockers writing guides and other materials. He has a degree in Game Design and Criticism.

Vehicles can be tough to come by in the early hours of GTA 6, and it doesn’t get much easier the farther into the game you get. Most every car you get has to be stolen in one way or another, especially after unlocking some new personal vehicles.

ATM machines hold a lot of cash in GTA 6. Learn how to break them open and steal everything inside with this guide.

There are a lot of good starter cars to register out there, but once you’re ready to expand, you might want something a little different. You won’t have an infinite amount of money, so you’ll need to be a little picky about what you want to keep.

Every vehicle on this list serves a good purpose and won’t run you into the ground money-wise, which is a nice bonus given your bank account problems. These are most of the general vehicles you can find around Port Gellhorn, although a couple are special finds.

Sometimes it’s nice to just have something a little fancy that’ll ride nice and easy down the streets. This Lowrider is by no means the faster or toughest car around, and it’s fairly average all around.

That’s what makes it a good extra car to have, because it’s fairly decent at everything. If you get it suped up, it can get much better, but since money is tight, it’s a relatively cheap option to buy, saving you some much-needed cash.

This one is a ton of fun to drive, mostly because it’s a pretty speedy vehicle on asphalt, but not so much on dirt. That’s really what drags the car down, but still it’s a nice car that’ll get you most anywhere in a jiffy.

If you’re a bit accident-prone, or prone to running into crazy NPCs, you may want to find something a bit sturdier. Still, it looks good and runs smoothly on asphalt, so it’s definitely one of the better vehicles on the road.

This car is a bit of an oddball for the area, as it’s clearly more of an upper-middle-class family car, which is not exactly what you think of in Port Gellhorn. It’s not a bad car for moving from point to point on the road or dirt.

It’s got pretty good handling and has some good size to it, making a good car for taking up space on the road. You won’t have to worry too much about getting hit with this big boy backing you up.

There are a lot of crazy looking cars on the road in GTA, but this is mostly a pretty normal-looking car. That said, it still can get going on the open road without wasting too much time, so as a getaway vehicle it’s not a bad choice.

It’s on the cheaper side and seemingly pretty abundant, so getting one shouldn’t be too difficult at this point in the game. The only real issue with the vehicle is that it’s got limited handling on both dirt and asphalt.

For the most part, you’re going to want a car over a bike, but when the moment for a bike comes, the Enduro is a great choice. It’s great for making a quick getaway on the road, provided you don’t crash into anything.

This one handles surprisingly nicely, but since it is a bike, you’re in a much more dangerous position to get hurt in an accident. Sounds silly, but when you’re holding a bag full of goodies, it’s not fun to lose it.

The Criminal Profile is GTA 6's version of an Honor system, and can change the game and how you play in major ways.

This is one chunky vehicle, but in a game like this, that comes in handy. It’s not bad on any terrain, and it can get up to speed pretty quickly, making it an excellent vehicle to go on a stealing spree with.

It can take a hit as good as it gives one, but its overall size might make squeezing through some tight streets a little difficult. It’s able to just move people out of the way with ease, but we all know that brings out the crazies.

While you’re mostly going to want something for the road in the early days, getting something that can do both is helpful. It’s not great on the road, but better than most, and it takes off from zero pretty quickly.

The major issue is that road handling is terrible, and the overall speed drops off pretty quickly; still, if you need to get off the road, this thing is great. You can even abuse it a bit since it’s a little stronger than most vehicles.

The Outlaw is one of the best and easiest-to-get vehicles in the game; while it might not be as nice as Paul Walker’s car, it does the job. Clearly a four-wheeler made for running off the road and making your own path.

It’s surprisingly good on both the dirt and road, but especially in the dirt, you can basically go wherever you want. It’s a beast, especially if you’re making your way through the swampy areas. It’s a bit expensive, but well worth the price.

One of the special vehicles you can find in a gang territory, this Caracara 4X4 is a phenomenal vehicle that really does it all. It’s got everything you might need in the early hours, and with some bonus strength, you can really push people around.

The only weak spot it has is that its asphalt handling is pretty bad, but who needs a road when you can just make your own? It’s a great car to keep Jason and Lucia happy and safe, without risking too much from either of them.

Another special vehicle you can steal from a gang hideout, the Firebug Dominator is an absolute godsend early on in the game. It’s got quick acceleration and some terrifying speed that’s only enhanced by the free nitro boost it comes with.

If there’s any car you need to have, it’s this one, if only because it can absolutely outrun most anyone or anything. You do have to be a little careful because of the speed, or you might find yourself off the highway and in the ocean meeting the Kraken.
